record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.original_question: Given a surface tessellation that approximates geometry to a prescribed chordal error but induces a very poor polyhedral metric, how can one compute a quasi-isometric flattening of the resulting extremely ill-conditioned triangulation so that the surface can be remeshed with nearly equilateral triangles and convergence-preserving patch-test behavior?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a piecewise smooth surface, and let $T$ be a triangulation (surface tessellation) whose vertices lie on $S$ and whose Hausdorff (chordal) distance to $S$ is at most a prescribed tolerance $\varepsilon > 0$. Equip $T$ with its induced polyhedral metric $g_T$ (the metric obtained by isometrically gluing the planar triangles). Assume $T$ is geometrically ill-conditioned in the sense that its triangles may have arbitrarily small minimum angles and that the aspect-ratio quality $Q(T) := \min_{t \in T} ho(t)/h(t)$ (in-radius over longest edge) may be arbitrarily close to $0$.

A quasi-isometric flattening of $(T, g_T)$ is a homeomorphism $\varphi : T 	o \Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$, piecewise affine on each triangle of $T$, whose quasi-isometric distortion
$$K(\varphi) := \operatorname*{ess\,sup}_{x \in T} \max\Big(\|D\varphi(x)\|_2,\; \|D\varphi(x)^{-1}\|_2\Big)$$
is bounded by a constant $K^\star$ depending only on the intrinsic geometry of $S$ (and not on the quality $Q(T)$).

Problem. Devise an algorithm that, given any such tessellation $T$ approximating $S$ to within chordal error $\varepsilon$, produces a quasi-isometric flattening $\varphi$ with $K(\varphi) \le K^\star$, in such a way that the image $\Omega = \varphi(T)$ can subsequently be remeshed into a triangulation $T'$ all of whose triangles are $\delta$-close to equilateral (i.e.\ all angles in $[\pi/3 - \delta, \pi/3 + \delta]$ for a prescribed $\delta > 0$), and such that the resulting remeshed surface $\varphi^{-1}(T')$ satisfies a finite-element patch test guaranteeing convergence of standard piecewise-linear approximations on it.

Prove existence of such an algorithm and provide explicit bounds on $K^\star$ in terms of the curvature and feature size of $S$, or show that no such algorithm exists under these hypotheses.
artifact.status_search_result: No specific solution to this exact formulation could be located. The problem of quasi-isometric flattening of arbitrarily ill-conditioned triangulations with guarantees independent of mesh quality remains a subject of active research in geometry processing and mesh generation (e.g., bounded-distortion parametrization, seamless parametrization), with partial results but no complete resolution under the stated hypotheses.

status_evidence.title: Bounded Distortion Parametrization
status_evidence.snippet: Work on parametrizations with bounded conformal/isometric distortion; guarantees depend on input mesh quality.
status_evidence.claim: Quasi-isometric flattening with mesh-quality-independent bounds remains an active research problem with only partial results.
